title: Divorce under personal religious law after a landmark constitutional ruling
p1:
Can a personal religious law decide everything about divorce? The answer may surprise you.

A landmark constitutional ruling changed how many people look at the balance between religious practices and fundamental rights.
p2: Many assume that personal laws operate completely outside constitutional scrutiny. But that is not always true. Courts have examined whether personal law practices violate basic rights and constitutional values.
p3:
The key takeaway is that personal religious laws can continue to govern many family matters, but they are not beyond legal review. When a practice affects equality, dignity, or individual rights, constitutional principles can become a deciding factor.

For anyone dealing with family disputes, this means knowing both your personal law and your constitutional protections matters.
conclusion: Do you think personal laws should have limits when they conflict with fundamental rights, or should religious autonomy remain the priority?
